---
# Copy to surveys/<year>/<short-name>.qmd. Files starting with "_" are not rendered.
title: "Short name"        # shown in the left menu: keep it to one line
link: "https://example.org/report"
link-text: "Publisher: title of the report"
who: "Who ran the survey"
when: "2025"
where: "Countries covered"
countries: eu27            # eu27 | euro-area | list of EU country codes, e.g. [DE, FR, IT] (EL = Greece); drives the sidebar country filter
asked: "Workers"           # Workers | Firms | Individuals | Workers and firms
sample: "Number of respondents"
use: work                  # work | private | both (asked separately) | any (not separated) | firm
# use-note: "optional short note, e.g. which split is published"
question: "\"The main AI question, in quotation marks if verbatim.\""
demographics:              # characteristics collected, shown as collapsible lists
  workers: [age, sex, education, occupation, sector, country]   # or individuals:
  firms: [size, sector, country]

aim: "One or two sentences on what the survey is for."
other-topics: "Job quality, working time, skills and training (topics besides AI)."

# Adoption tracking, used for the time series on the overview page.
# Leave out adoption-workers / adoption-firms if the survey has no such question.
month: "2025-03"           # middle month of fieldwork
adoption-individuals: 35   # % of all individuals using AI for any purpose
adoption-workers: 30       # % of workers using AI at work; aim for employed people aged 21-64
adoption-base: "workers aged 16-65"   # population the worker figure refers to
adoption-firms: 20         # % of firms using AI
coverage: eu27             # eu27 | euro-area | eu-subset (10+ EU countries) | few (under 10 countries)
# series: my-survey        # same value on every wave of a repeated survey, to join the dots
# label-pos: below        # right | above | below, if the label collides on the overview chart
# chart-label: "Label"     # label on the overview chart, if different from title
---
